abstract: Verbatim transcripts, which keep the hesitations and interactional particles that ordinary automatic speech recognition (ASR) removes, are a prerequisite for speech-based cognitive assessment, and they are hardest to obtain for languages with little annotated speech. We study this problem for Swedish with a 1.02-hour corpus of manually transcribed spontaneous speech, too small for full fine-tuning of KB-Whisper-large. We adapt the model with a low-rank adapter and compare three ways of extending the training data: pseudo-labeling of untranscribed in-domain audio, unguided synthesis with a language model and a text-to-speech system, and a gold-preserving pipeline that reproduces the disfluency distribution of the gold corpus by construction and can be audited before training. Fine-tuning reduces disfluency-segment word error rate (WER) by 32% relative, with blockwise-bootstrap confidence intervals disjoint from the zero-shot baseline, while the three augmentation strategies are not separable by WER across five seeds. The gold-preserving pipeline needs no untranscribed audio, and its disfluency distribution can be verified in advance.
oneSentenceThesis: 针对仅 1.02 小时瑞典语逐字金标导致大模型抑制迟疑的问题，论文以低秩适配器微调并对比伪标注、无引导合成与金标保留合成，发现微调降低迟疑片段 WER（词错误率）约 32% 且区间与基线分离，而三种扩增均值不可区分且 2.35:1 放大会退化，代价是仅 6 个测试文件与 5 个种子下的高方差与无人工听测。
originalTitle: Gold-Preserving Synthetic Augmentation for Verbatim Swedish Automatic Speech Recognition
readerTitle: 金标保留合成如何为瑞典语逐字识别补足迟疑分布
